# DRAFT: Medical device adverse incident report

> This is a draft for human review. It has not been submitted. A manufacturer would report through the MHRA MORE portal; healthcare professionals and users report through the Yellow Card scheme.

## 1. Device
- Name: ClinicDrift-monitored DR screening model
- Version: v1.0
- Intended use: screening retinal photographs for referable diabetic retinopathy

## 2. Where and when
- Clinic: SW-MES-01 (EyePACS, then Messidor-2, Simulated)
- Period: week 9 (starting 2026-03-02)

## 3. What happened
ClinicDrift identified that retinal scans from clinic SW-MES-01 no longer match the image distribution on which the AI model was validated (drift score 0.99, where 0.5 indicates similarity to training data and 1 indicates a clear difference).

Because expert grades for the 50 scans acquired this week have not yet arrived, the catch rate (sensitivity for referable disease) cannot be verified. The AI is referring more patients than expected: 86% of this week's scans were referred, compared to 68% of the training scans.

## 4. Potential patient impact
Because the catch rate cannot be verified, the number of potentially missed cases cannot be estimated. No patient harm has been confirmed.

## 5. Likely cause
Significant reduction in image quality, sharpness, and contrast alongside an increase in image resolution due to a change in fundus camera hardware or image acquisition protocol at clinic SW-MES-01 (category: camera or image quality; confidence 85%; source: gemini).

Evidence:
- Drift score reached 0.99, indicating a severe distribution shift from training data.
- Mean image quality decreased from 0.5 in training to 0.193 (-61.4% relative change).
- Mean sharpness dropped from 0.000399 to 0.000222 (-44.3% relative change).
- Mean contrast decreased from 0.00963 in training to 0.0548 (-43.1% relative change).
- Mean image resolution increased from 1020.0 px to 2070.0 px (+101.9% relative change).
- Mean referral score increased from 0.193 to 0.299 (+55.1% relative change), and referral rate rose from 0.685 to 0.86 (+25.6% relative change).
- The weekly scan volume is small (50 scans), making evidence moderately limited in statistical power.

## 6. Action
ClinicDrift paused the AI model at this clinic because image data has drifted beyond validated limits, meaning the catch rate cannot be verified. It is recommended that scans from this clinic are sent for human grading until the following checks are complete:

Checks:
- [ ] Inspect the fundus camera lens for smudges, dust, or degradation.
- [ ] Verify if a new fundus camera model or resolution setting was recently introduced at the clinic.
- [ ] Audit staff image capture protocols, ensuring proper focusing and illumination during acquisition.
- [ ] Check input image pre-processing and quality assessment filters in the deployment pipeline.

## 7. Regulatory context
- Post-market surveillance (PMS): this alarm is part of ongoing monitoring of the device in use.
- Predetermined change control plan (PCCP): any model change made in response should fall within an agreed PCCP.
- MHRA AI Airlock Phase 2 report: see recommendations 3 and 4.

## 8. MIT AI Risk Repository tags
- 7.3 AI system safety, failures & limitations > Lack of capability or robustness
- 1.3 Discrimination & toxicity > Unequal performance across groups
- 5.1 Human-computer interaction > Overreliance and unsafe use
